messages:
ops-bot: Pager — high rate of GPU driver resets observed on rwd-prod-us-west-2 cluster. automated detection at 1967504321, creating thread.
ops-bot: Symptoms: node flaps, container crashes, OOMs on serving pods, Xid 13/31 spikes, increased ECC counts. Affected nodes: gpu-np-05, gpu-np-06, gpu-np-08.
Alex K: oncall here, pulling logs from gpu-np-05 and 06. please tag me for any routing changes.
Maria C: dmesg shows repeated NVRM Xid messages and GPU fallen off bus. looks like memory/driver level instability. snippet:
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, pid=1234, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12346.001234] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13, GPU has resumed but ECC volatile errors increasing
[ 12346.002345] kernel: GPU device 0000:65:00: pci_bus error severity: Corrected
```
Jin L: cordoning gpu-np-05 now: `kubectl cordon gpu-np-05` then drain (ignore daemonsets).
Sam R: attempting soft driver restart on gpu-np-06: `systemctl restart nvidia-driver.service` — FYI will report back within 2m.
Maria C: please don't reboot unless restart fails. restarting can drop KV caches and increase latency.
Sam R: driver restart completed, logs still show Xid 13 within 30s. not stable.
Ira P: CS update: flagging customers using hosted-inference tier for potential degraded responses; outreach initiated to 3 customers. No indicators of data exfiltration.
Alex K: mitigation plan: 1) divert non-critical traffic to dedicated-pool-1, 2) reduce batch sizes and increase per-request timeouts, 3) remove scheduling onto affected nodes. initiating route change.
ops-bot: Applying routing policy: `route apply --from=hosted-api --to=dedicated-pool-1 --pct=40` (in progress).
deploy-bot: Canary shift executed: 10% -> 40% to dedicated-pool-1.
Jin L: `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,UTILIZATION` on gpu-np-08 shows high temp + volatile ECC counts:
```
GPU 0
    Temperature
        GPU Current Temp                      : 92 C
    ECC Errors
        Volatile                               : 12
        Aggregate                              : 54
```
Maria C: persistent ECC counts + Xid spikes = likely hardware fault. recommend RMA for nodes with sustained errors.
Sam R: will schedule cordon+drain+rebuild for gpu-np-05/06/08 if errors persist after tonight's checks.
Alex K: temporarily adjusted autoscaler to avoid placing serving pods on gpu-np-05/06/08: `autoscaler exclude-nodes --label=gpu-unstable`
Ira P: notified impacted customers: message sent - "We've detected transient GPU instability causing brief degradation for some requests. Traffic has been routed to dedicated capacity and engineers are remediating. We'll follow up with timeline."
Maria C: collecting full logs and metrics, dumping kernel traces to incident bucket: `s3://incidents/1967504321/` — adding to runbook.
Sam R: opening hardware ticket for RMA with cloud provider referencing ECC spikes and Xid history.
Alex K: quick check - any recent driver or kernel changes pushed in last 48h?
Jin L: none in prod kernel or driver. only a serving model shard redeploy ~3h ago but that shouldn't cause ECC.
Maria C: next steps for oncall handoff: 1) ensure cordon/drain finished, 2) confirm fallback routing stable and p95 latency acceptable, 3) monitor Xid/ECC counters for reduction, 4) progress RMA and replacement timeline.
Sam R: leaving notes for night team: if node shows sustained Xid > 5/min after driver restart, mark for rebuild. Avoid live reboots unless hardware team approves.
oncall: taking over at 1967508000 — acknowledged. Will run healthcheck script every 15m and post updates here.
Ira P: keeping CS looped, will send an update after next confirmation of stable failover.
Maria C: post-incident action items: (a) tighten Xid alert threshold to catch earlier, (b) run integration tests for driver restart handling, (c) evaluate thermal telemetry alerting and fan curves.
ops-bot: Incident state: mitigations applied, hardware RMA opened, traffic redistributed. Will post scheduled updates. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
